The establishment instruction describes an ascending ramp: start with the lightest available load and add the smallest increment between preparatory sets while at least the target reserve remains with stable technique; the working load is the heaviest such load; load and convention are recorded.
No kilogram is derived from sex, body mass, another exercise or implement; a stale or differently configured known load is only a hint or ceiling.

After establishment, a load or repetition step requires a logged set record meeting target repetitions with reserve >= prescribed RIR - 1; otherwise the dose holds. A logged load above the planned load is adopted only when that exposure meets this criterion and only up to one smallest increment above the plan, never above a re-establishment ceiling; otherwise the planned load stays the reference and the logged load is asked about. A logged load at or below the plan is executed evidence; a changed known load is a modification (D44).
RIR is treated as approximate (about one repetition of error); technique and comfort govern continuation and stopping.
Fail-closed: no ESTABLISH rows are emitted when this boundary is not enabled.

A load logged on an establishment row becomes a prescribed numeric (KNOWN) load only after the athlete confirms it (in kilograms or pounds, in the planned convention), after a second logged exposure of the exercise in a separate session (later, or earlier in the same week) within establishmentAgreementIncrements smallest increment of it, or when it lies within one smallest increment of the athlete's own load hint in the same convention. Until then the next exposure is FROM_LOG with no number, its instructions describe effort-guided selection only and never point to the logged value (D48), and the logged value is asked about. Numeric plausibility of a confirmed or repeated value is Data-owned (D45).

Loads are kilograms in the engine: a pound value (intake or log) converts at the nearest 0.5 kg and keeps the reported value; another or missing unit, or a logged convention different from the planned one, is never adopted and is asked about; no prescription carries pounds or a known load above 500 kg.

An above-plan logged load is adopted only when that exercise's gate for the week is ADVANCE or EARNED; a missing reps-in-reserve log, an adverse response or a converging-fatigue hold keeps the planned load and the load is asked about (D44).

Establishment needs an executed exposure with a logged load: an establishment exposure that was missed, dated inside a declared pause, reported only in a conflicted report, or performed without a usable logged load establishes no load, so the next exposure is again the effort-guided establishment row (at most the establishment set count at RIR >= 3, the ramp-up, no load, no progression step), under the earlier ceiling when there is one; a FROM_LOG row exists only for an exercise with a logged load (pending or adopted) and never says 'use the load you logged' without one. Until a review sees the exercise performed with a logged load, its later exposures in the same week are the establishment row too, and two establishment logs of that week within one increment confirm each other (D45; dossier Q1). D52, resolved in round 11.

An exercise not performed for more than return.moderateMaxDays, counted in calendar days from its last executed exposure to the date of the session being built (the completed-work ledger at reviews; for an intake known dose, its observedAt; in a projection, the planned date), restarts with effort-guided establishment with its last logged load as a ceiling, whether the absence came from rotation, a substitution window, skipped sessions or a return. Each session is judged on its own date, and no unexecuted exposure counts (dossier Q4). Its earlier set count, including any block-boundary set, comes back at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, never at once, whatever the state's mode at the re-establishment (known load, pending establishment log or unlogged), and the re-establishment row itself never exceeds the reduced dose of a taper, race-window or post-event session (strength.resumeAfterDays and setsAfterReestablishment; D52 resolved in round 11; D53 resolved in round 12 for a known-load state and still open for a from-log state; D54 open; both required before FREEZE-2).

A session reported completed without exercise details counts as performed for every exercise of that session (the resume clock) but is no load evidence: a new loaded exercise is established again, a known lift keeps its load without a step, and a from-log exercise without a usable logged load is established again by effort under its earlier ceiling. A partial report counts only the exercises it lists (dossier Q2).

An intake known dose was last performed on its observedAt date, which must be the date the dose was last performed, not the date it was reported; its resume clock starts there, so a dose observed close to the 28-day intake limit can be re-established at its first program exposure (dossier Q3).
A conflicted execution report performs nothing and neither sets nor confirms a load until it is corrected (QRE-R6-14; author-found with D52).

Interruption reasons are structured; any illness, injury, pain or clinical category, or a whole-word clinical-lexicon match in free text, routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED regardless of nonclinical or clinicalReason flags; an ambiguous or missing reason is ASK; the same rule applies to the intake pause and the legacy path.
Current eligibility must be assessed on or after the interruption end date.
SHORT (<= shortMaxDays): resume the last executed doses; the first quality slot runs easy; the next step waits for executed sessions.

MODERATE (<= moderateMaxDays): run entry from a current demonstration (modality RUN, easy/long/recovery-easy family, completed, conversational effort, compatible response, ordinary and next-day function, observed after the interruption began and within currentDemonstrationMaxAgeDays) or the reviewed 15-minute entry; at most moderateStepsToPrior conditional steps to the prior executed dose, each within the single-run ceiling of R6-PLANNED-PROGRESSION.

Strength return: every strength exposure of the return-entry week, including exercises first set up in it, is strengthEntrySets set(s) at RIR >= strengthEntryMinimumRir with the prior load only as a ceiling. Return step 2 is max(1, min(ceiling - 1, strengthEntrySets + 1)) sets at RIR 3, the ceiling being the last set count executed before the break outside a return step and outside a phase reduction (else the known count, else the normal count). Afterwards the count comes back at most one set per executed week without a phase reduction, up to the ceiling (a phase-reduced step 2 is followed by the step-2 count itself), and goes above it only through a later development block with no return-step exposure. Consolidation, specific, taper, race-week and post-event reductions apply on top, in the return steps too. Return-entry and return-step exposures never count toward a block-boundary set increase. During the return steps a logged load is capped at the current return reference (the load before the break until an entry log is adopted, then the adopted entry load) and asked about; the prior KNOWN load is prescribed only after a post-interruption logged entry load supports it, otherwise FROM_LOG from the entry log (D49; operational.return.strengthReturnSets, returnLoadCap).

LONG (> moderateMaxDays): restart class for running, with the achieved run peaks and the longest continuous run cleared so that taper, race-week, race-day and next-block doses and the race-day statement come only from runs executed after the restart (operational.return.restartRunHistory); strength re-establishes by effort; no prior-load KNOWN prescription until a post-interruption log exists.
EARNED is unavailable during RETURN/RESTART; surplus counts only observations after the return started.
No universal percentage rollback; historical maxima are ceilings, not current proof.

A nonclinical return requires a structured nonclinical reason category (legacy R5 contract: clinicalReason=false) and current eligibility assessed on or after the interruption end with every clinical flag false; free text can only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes.

Interruption facts out of range or contradicting each other (days outside 1-3650 or not whole, unreal dates, start after end, dates after the review, days and dates disagreeing by more than one day) are asked, never resolved to the least conservative class; a clinical flag that means yes in any form routes to a human, one that is neither yes nor no is asked.
A run demonstration shorter than run.minimumSessionMinutes is not used as a demonstration.

Additions to the free-text screen (clinical terms, phrases, the damage-verb plus body-part rule) may only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes; body parts alone stay ASK; a damage statement whose every damage verb is locally negated is ASK, never NONCLINICAL; a negation elsewhere in the clause never hides an affirmed damage statement.

A clinical eligibility flag that means yes in any form routes CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED in the intake, the review and the legacy path, as does a clinical status in any letter case; any other non-boolean flag leaves eligibility unassessed (ASK), never clearance and never assumed illness.
The round-8 lexical additions (R11) only add CLINICAL or ASK outcomes; 'Paternity leave' and 'Funeral and grief' stay nonclinical; conservative false positives are owned-gap residuals.

The return ends for every exercise: an exercise not used during the return steps carries no return step once the exercises in use complete theirs, and rotation resumes on its cadence afterwards. In use means prescribed in the week, executed or not: a missed in-use exposure keeps its exercise at its step and the return open, and a week without strength exposure ends nothing (D51, resolved in round 10; dossier Q2).

An exercise that reappears after a return without having been performed during it is established by effort when it was never performed (including one first prescribed in a session dated inside the pause) and re-established by effort when it was last performed more than return.moderateMaxDays earlier, counted from its last executed exposure (D52, resolved in round 11).

A never-performed exercise prescribed during a return gets the return-entry dose while any exercise in use is at the entry step and, once performed, joins the return at that step; if every exercise in use has passed the entry step, it is established by effort (at most 2 sets at RIR >= 3) and then progresses as a new exercise. The second case is to be declared in the next policy revision (R17).

Weekly-review contract: these bindings hold when every elapsed week receives a gating weekly review, in order and after its last session, with unreported sessions reviewed as missed. A week that receives no gating review keeps the projection's assumption that it was executed and logged (establishment, progression, block credit, achieved peaks and the strength resume clock); that path is outside this approval and must be closed before any use beyond the offline reference (R18).
limitations: Direct evidence on nonclinical pause-length dosing is sparse; length classes are operational.
Cause verification relies on self-report.

The interruption-reason text screen is a lexicon heuristic; any further lexical residual is an owned open gap, and the structured category plus current eligibility (dated after the break, every clinical flag false) remain the primary defence.
Pregnancy and postpartum are excluded at intake by a structured field, but a review or return has no structured re-check; free text is the only backstop there (R11).
Phase-reduced weeks do not raise the return count, so a return across consolidation or taper weeks takes longer.
A block containing any return exposure earns no set: the boundary set can wait up to one more block (probe X: 3 sets through week 15 after a break in week 4).
Pregnancy and postpartum status is not asked again at reviews or returns (R11, second half; Product/Data).
A bodyweight exercise rotated back after a return resumes its earlier set count at RIR 3 without a re-establishment step (R17).
A never-performed exercise first performed after every exercise in use has passed the return entry is not held to the return steps (R17); not observed in the probed timelines.

Strength stays at a reduced dose: taper sets about taperStrengthSetFraction of the preceding dose at RIR >= 3; race week one session of raceWeekStrengthSets at RIR >= raceWeekStrengthMinimumRir no later than raceWeekStrengthMinDaysBeforeRace days before the race; no new exercise, load increase or rotation.

Post-event: no running before postEventFirstRunMinDaysAfterRace days; runs optional and easy within postEventEasyMinutes; one light strength session; redevelopment (NEXT_BLOCK) requires an eligibility and function assessment dated after the race; redevelopment fractions are declared in the policy.

Event proximity counts days to the race (raceWindowDays 6; 7 taper days per taper week before the window): race-window sessions have no long run and no quality, an optional shakeout the day before, at most one race-effort touch on the run day closest to the race that is >= raceWeekTouchMinDaysBeforeRace days out, and short easy runs; taper-day sessions take taper doses whichever calendar week they fall in; post-race sessions follow the post-event rules by days since the race; a race date marked unavailable is asked about.
In WALK_JOG or RESTART mode, taper-day, race-window and post-event run sessions are reductions or holds of the achieved session of that mode, never a continuous run the mode has not reached (D43a).

Race day is a completion prescription at conversational effort with walk breaks (jog bouts no longer than achieved), without strides and without an instruction to press, when the race-week mode is WALK_JOG, RESTART or RETURN, when the athlete was in WALK_JOG or RESTART mode in any week of the program before the race (D47), or for a half marathon whose achieved long run is below raceDayCompletion.halfMarathonAchievedLongRunBelowMinutes; race-day warm-up strides and shakeout strides for any athlete only after executed strides (D43b-c, R9).

Whenever race day is a completion, the program or the proposal carries the non-blocking negotiation, recomputed from the race-week state of every proposal (added, replaced or removed), stating the longest continuous run executed by race week (never 0 when such a run was counted; a restart after a long interruption starts the count again), why race day is a completion, and both options (keep the event with walk breaks; a later or shorter event) (D43d, D47).
In taper weeks and at the start of the next block the long run is never shorter than that week's easy run (R10).
Walk/jog and restart steps do not advance on taper, race-window or post-event days; the next block resumes the walk/jog ladder one step back.
No exemption from the history-based completion applies unless it is declared and reviewed (D47c).

dossierAnswers.question: D53 fix (the round-11 finding): after a performed re-establishment the count, block-boundary set included, comes back from the re-establishment count one set per executed week without a phase reduction.
dossierAnswers.answer: Resolved for a known-load state. Probe AH: 0 of 584 next exposures more than one set above the re-establishment and none more than one above the count before the gap; probe AHb finds the round-11 120 on the reviewed round-11 runtime, so the probe still detects the defect. Probe AI follows every later exposure of 2,448 re-establishments in 384 timelines: no count above the allowance, none held below it, and every trace reaches the normal count (1,872 after 1 week, 384 after 2 weeks, 144 after 3 weeks) or ends with the program. The cap is cleared by a return, restarted by a second gap and not advanced by a held week (probe AL). My diff equals the author's.

dossierAnswers.question: Disclosed: the cap rises only in an executed week (ADVANCE gate with logged evidence); a week performed without a usable log, or held, does not advance the regain.
dossierAnswers.answer: Accepted. It is the rule I set in round 11 and the D49 return cap, and it matches how every other step counts executed work (QRE-R6-04). Probe AL: a re-establishment week held by a missed later session keeps 2 sets the next week, then 3.

dossierAnswers.question: Disclosed: a block set earned in a consolidation week waits for the next week without a phase reduction while the cap still binds.
dossierAnswers.answer: Accepted. A consolidation week steps volume back, so it should not also count toward regaining volume after a break; the cost is one set for a week (probes AB, AF and AI). The same pause holds through specific and taper weeks, which is conservative.

dossierAnswers.question: Found in round 12: is the fix complete for every state an exercise can be in when it is re-established?
dossierAnswers.answer: No: D53 stays open for a from-log state. The cap is set only in the branch that converts a known load, so an exercise whose establishment log is still pending (D45), or that was performed without a usable log, regains a block-boundary set at once after a re-establishment: 48 of 1,224 next exposures in the noisy-log grid, 24 of them prescribed 2 -> 4 sets; probe AJ reproduces it on the current runtime (4x5 after 2 sets) and on the reviewed round-11 runtime. Required: start the regain at every performed re-establishment whatever the state's mode.

dossierAnswers.question: Found in round 12: are re-establishments held to the reduced dose of event phases?
dossierAnswers.answer: No: D54. The re-establishment row (2 sets at RIR >= 3) is returned before the phase reduction, so in race week, the taper and the post-event week it exceeds the declared dose (70 rows in probe AK; race week 2 sets at RIR 3 against 1 set at RIR >= 4, six days before the race). It contradicts principle 8, operational.event and EVENT-TRANSITION conditions 7 and 8. The weight is low to modest (R6-S53 to R6-S56), but it is the window the reduced dose exists for. Required: apply the phase reduction to the re-establishment row.
